title: migration-diagnostics-toolkit-changelog-webhooks-and-sample-suite
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a developer-facing migration diagnostics toolkit and automated changelog pipeline to smooth v1->v2 SDK migrations across Python/TypeScript/Go. Deliverables: (1) CLI 'redwood-sdk-check' that scans a repository to detect deprecated API usage patterns, streaming ergonomics mismatches, and retry/idempotency anti-patterns; (2) a sample-suite repo with end-to-end examples demonstrating recommended v2 patterns for streaming, retries, and backoff across Python/TS/Go; (3) a git-hook/CI step that extracts deprecation annotations from SDK source and generates structured changelog fragments (JSON) consumable by the Console release notes and GitHub releases; (4) webhook-based changelog publish integration to the Console docs site and Slack release channel for visibility.
acceptance_criteria: CLI can scan a sample repo and output a migration report with at least 10 rule detections (deprecated methods, streaming -> iterator mismatch, missing idempotency tokens)
Sample-suite contains three language folders (python, typescript, go) with runnable examples and README migration notes
CI job demonstrates automated changelog fragment generation from SDK source annotations in a demo PR
Docs team approves release notes integration and templates for generated changelog fragments
Performance sanity: CLI scan runs under 6s on a 200-file repo in CI (optimize later if needed)
notes: Initial spike validated AST-based detection for TS/Python and go/ast for Go; prototype flagged common streaming misuse (awaiting more patterns from DX)
Trade-offs discussed: deep static analysis vs heuristic regexes. Decided to start with a hybrid approach: lightweight AST rules for high-confidence patterns + regex heuristics for quick wins
Will include a --fix flag for certain patterns (imports rename, simple API call rewrites) but defer aggressive autofix to future iteration due to risk
Integration plan: CI step runs 'redwood-sdk-check --format json' and persists artifacts; a small GH Action converts those into PR comments and optional release fragments
Security: CLI runs in user CI; no secrets required. Confirmed no PII extraction. security_review_required=false
